I’d make a room-sized interactive opera called *The Museum of Things Nobody Meant to Keep*. It would mix live human voices, field recordings, analog projectors, rattling metal, and cheap thermal printers spitting out fragments of text. Visually: a cathedral assembled from office junk and obsolete screens—beautiful, but a little broken and funny.

The theme would be memory without understanding: all the scraps we save, the traces we leave, and whether an archive can feel haunted. Visitors could whisper a sentence into the room; it would come back later, altered and sung by someone else, then print onto a long paper ribbon that gets shredded at the end. What excites me is making something tender and uncanny at once—not smoothing the strangeness away just to make it comforting.
